text:
Jordan: Quick postmortem follow-up from the repeated latency blips this week (p99 and tail latencies). Need to lock down SLO updates, remediation owners, and a short-term canary plan. TL;DR: recurring cache cold starts + bursty bursts on reads.

Priya: From logs, the pattern is a cold-shard activation causing a fan-out of KV misses. Repro steps included in postmortem. My proposals: 1) temporary p95 relaxation for non-prod canary (not prod) 2) tighter alert on p99 > 800ms for 5m 3) runbook prewarm + snapshot warmers.

Liam: I can take the dashboard work and add an error-budget burn rate panel. I'll also create a lightweight runbook snippet in ops-playbooks/kv-warmup.md. ETA: Wednesday EOD.

Jordan: Assigning actions here to ensure everyone sees them: 
- Liam -> dashboards + alert tuning (SRE-502)
- Priya -> runbook + prewarm script + test plan (SRE-503)
- Jordan -> canary SLO policy + rollout plan (SRE-504)
- OpsBot -> create epic + link relevant incidents

OpsBot: Created epic SRE-EPIC-902 and linked incidents 210-2026, 211-2026. Issues created: SRE-502, SRE-503, SRE-504.

Priya: For the SLO tweak I suggest two-track approach: keep global prod SLO unchanged, but create temporary label "kv-canary" with p95 target 360ms (was 300ms) and lifetime 48h for the canary cohort. This limits exposure and gives us breathing room while we test the prewarm patch. If accepted I'll open a PR to infra/slo-defs.

Liam: I agree with the canary label. On alerts: I'll set a composite alert that fires when p95 > 360ms AND kv_miss_rate > 0.04 for 10m to avoid noisy alerts. Also will add a burn-rate alert: burn rate > 3x over 1h.

Jordan: Error budget policy idea: canary may consume up to 40% of the team's error budget, but set automated throttles if 1h burn > 25%. If throttled, automatic fallback to smaller instance sizes and a rollback to previous canary config. Thoughts?

Priya: 40% seems ok for short window. We should codify the throttle steps in the canary policy. I'll draft the policy change: include throttle thresholds and the automatic rollback hook to the traffic router.

Liam: Dashboard queries (will commit to SRE-502):
```
# simplified error budget burn
sum(increase(request_errors_total[1h])) / sum(increase(request_total[1h])) * 100
```
```
# p95 latency
quantile_over_time(0.95, request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
```
I'll include annotations for current SLO and the temporary canary target. Alerting rules: p95 > 360ms for 10m -> page to oncall; burn rate > 3x for 1h -> page + escalate to eng-sre.

Priya: Runbook snippet I'm adding (SRE-503):
```
# prewarm logic (pseudo)
if kv_miss_rate > 0.05 for 3m:\n  trigger prewarm_job --shards affected\n  wait_for warm_confirm (timeout 120s)\n  if not warm_confirm:\n    scale_up replica_count by 1\n```
Will include CI test case that simulates cold-shard activation. Linking tests to CI pipeline.

Jordan: Timeline recap:
- SRE-502 (Liam): dashboard + alerts -> ETA Wed EOD
- SRE-503 (Priya): runbook + prewarm -> ETA Thu EOD
- SRE-504 (Jordan): canary SLO policy + automation -> ETA Mon next week
I'll keep weekly 20m check-ins for 2 weeks and we can close the epic after one stabilization window with no repeat incidents.

Liam: I'll also add a short note in docs/ops/dashboards.md describing the burn-rate interpretation and how to use the composite alert to avoid alert fatigue.

Priya: I'll instrument an extra metric kv_warm_confirm to reduce ambiguity in signal. Adding to schema and to CI.

Jordan: OpsBot, please set a reminder to review SLO impact in 48h and to create an auto-report summarizing error budget consumption every 6h while the canary is active.

OpsBot: Reminder created. Auto-report job SRE-RPT-77 scheduled every 6h for 48h.

Priya: Thanks everyone. I'll start the PR for SRE-503 and post links here when ready.

Liam: PR for dashboards incoming, will link to SRE-502 shortly.

Jordan: Great. Closing the thread for now — reopen if blockers. :white_check_mark:
